problem: Cross-chain activity involves different networks, wallets, fees and protocol rules. Etherway brings swaps, token and NFT transfers, and gas refuelling into one application.
contribution: I built Etherway end to end, including the interface and its integrations.

architecture.title: Application interface
architecture.text: Next.js and TypeScript components manage network and token selection, quotes, wallet state and transaction-status views.

architecture.title: Protocol integrations
architecture.text: Squid routing and provider-specific LayerZero V2 and Hyperlane handlers handle route execution, fee quotes and contract calls.

architecture.title: Application data
architecture.text: Prisma models a PostgreSQL data layer for users, interactions, referrals and project/task records.

decisions.title: Separate quoting, execution and status
decisions.text: The bridge keeps route-fetching, transaction-execution and status-modal state separate. That makes an asynchronous cross-chain operation visible as more than a single button click.

decisions.title: Keep protocol rules in adapters
decisions.text: Provider-specific handlers contain differences in fee quoting and contract calls. This keeps those differences out of the shared interface, while leaving separate integration paths to maintain.

decisions.title: Reconcile dependent network selections
decisions.text: The gas-refuel interface checks valid destination networks when the source changes and resets an incompatible selection. Network choice changes the valid operation, not just its label.

verification: The public repository includes the bridge interface, refuelling flow, protocol adapters and database models. The source links below show each part.
